text:
deploy-bot: MANUAL APPROVAL: Production deploy queued for service `inference-runtime`.
Details: tag `release/2.3.1-hotfix` (commit `c9f2a4b`), changelog: hotfix for mem leak in KV cache. CI: ✅ all checks passed. Canary: 10% for 15m. Rollback: auto + manual rollback route to `release/2.3.0`.
Change window: 23:00-02:00 PST. Requesting prod-gate approval.

sanjay: quick Q — does this touch the routing layer or just runtime? impact on dedupe? 

deploy-bot: runtime-only, no routing. Affects KV cache eviction and attention cache; we've run load test with 1k rps.

emily: approve from infra side. :white_check_mark:

julia: can you pin the worker image to `sha256:3a7f...`? don't want drift during rollout.

deploy-bot: image pinned to `sha256:3a7f9d2b6e`. Thanks.

mike-oncall: I'm oncall and approve — go ahead. I'll monitor. :eyes:

deploy-bot: APPROVED — starting canary deployment to prod (10% traffic) now. Commits: `c9f2a4b` · CI: https://ci.redwood/inference/4321

deploy-bot: Canary progress: deployed to 12 hosts, avg latency +2ms, error-rate +0.9% (within SLOs). Continuing.

deploy-bot: Canary alert: error-rate rising — now +3.2% vs baseline, spike correlated with `kv_eviction` logs. Threshold breach.

sanjay: Can we throttle canary to 0% and pause? Rollback if no quick fix.

emily: Agree, recommend rollback. No quick patch that's safe.

mike-oncall: I authorize rollback. Rolling back to `release/2.3.0`.

deploy-bot: Initiating rollback to `release/2.3.0` — draining canary hosts and shifting traffic back.

deploy-bot: Rollback complete. Prod stable on `release/2.3.0`. Error-rate back to baseline. Incident created: INC-2026-409 (link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-409)

julia: thanks. Please add pinned image and config diff to the incident and schedule a postmortem.

release-bot: Noted. Scheduling postmortem and blocking `release/2.3.1-hotfix` until root cause and E2E tests updated. cc: @sanjay @emily @mike-oncall

mike-oncall: good call. reopening the hotfix branch for fixes.

sanjay: I'll take the root cause and follow up. Thanks everyone.
